title: Cookie MCP
shortDescription: The onchain execution layer for AI agents on Cookie Chain.
description: Cookie MCP is a Model Context Protocol server that enables AI agents to interact directly with Cookie Chain. Agents can execute swaps, launch tokens, provide liquidity, stake assets, bridge tokens, inspect balances, and interact with supported DeFi protocols through a unified interface.

title: Crumbs
shortDescription: The utility app for Cookie Chain: holder snapshots, airdrops, wallet cleanup, swaps by link, .cook names, and a clicker that mints CRUMB.
description: Crumbs is an installable web app with the tools every token community on Cookie Chain ends up needing. Snapshot pulls every holder of a token from the Cookiescan DAS index, folded by wallet with pools and vaults flagged, and gives you a concentration bar, a sortable table, a CSV and a share card. Airdrop sends COOK or any SPL or Token-2022 token to that snapshot or to a pasted list, same amount for everyone or pro-rata, packed into as few transactions as fit, with missing token accounts created, one wallet prompt, and live confirmations with Cookiescan links. Cleanup revokes delegates and closes empty token accounts so the rent comes back. Swap by link packs a two-sided token trade into one transaction against a durable nonce, so two wallets can trade with no escrow and no pool. A .cook name works wherever Crumbs asks for a wallet (airdrop recipients, the swap counterparty), and wallets that set a primary name show it on the leaderboard, in holder tables and in the wallet button, read straight from the name service program. Crumb Clicker is an idle clicker where every click is a Cookie Chain transaction, signed by a browser session key after one wallet approval; each UTC day's totals settle on chain and split a fixed pool of CRUMB, the app's proof-of-play token, minted only through the emission program with a hard cap and supply-triggered halvings. Two Anchor programs deployed on Cookie Chain mainnet run the game and the mint: crumb_clicker 7aPZt6exe1H2A1fnSqV2kV2ZHpgQWtKe4LYEXv1x3Lqi and crumb_emission C8NRjLU9ajS5okBSbDhMBXsF2naVGm82y6g3hdefTQcY. Nothing runs on a backend: reads come from rpc.cookiescan.io and api.cookiescan.io, and every write is a transaction the user's Nightly wallet signs.

title: Sprinkle
shortDescription: Payment links, tip jars and a receipts dashboard on Cookie Chain. No backend, wallet-native, .cook names supported.
description: Sprinkle lets anyone get paid on Cookie Chain with a link or QR code. The creator picks a recipient (an address or a .cook name), COOK or any registry token, an optional amount, a label and a message; the whole request is encoded in the URL so links never expire and nothing is stored anywhere. The payer opens the link, connects Nightly, sees their balance and USD estimate, and pays: a SystemProgram transfer for COOK or an idempotent ATA create plus transferChecked for SPL and Token-2022, always with a sprinkle:v1:<label> memo. The transaction is simulated first for readable errors, signed by the wallet, broadcast by the page to rpc.cookiescan.io and confirmed with live stage updates and an explorer link. The Received tab reads any address's history straight from the chain, extracts incoming transfers, groups Sprinkle payments by label, totals them in USD via Cookiescan prices and charts them per day. .cook names are resolved on-chain at payment time through the cookie_domains program, so a payment follows the name; names sitting in the marketplace escrow are refused rather than paid into a program account.

title: Cookie Tab
shortDescription: Pay any Cookie Chain invoice from the token you actually hold. USD or COOK links; Cookiebox + Candy Shop swap verified in the browser; public receipts from chain memos.
description: Cookie Tab makes invoices and tip jars on Cookie Chain that a payer can settle from the token they actually hold. A payer holding the wrong token gets quotes from both the Cookiebox and Candy Shop aggregators, the winning route is simulated and checked against their own balances, and the swap and the payment go to their wallet as one transaction that lands together or not at all (on chain: cookiescan.io/tx/3R1C9BBUH3K42jGQHfP5qSqkx4p4hxeWZyva5c5hHERogspxRnkK2X1C3pwAXKVvFYEykoG1ZWXvBhzxffnp5hFL, a Cookiebox swap plus a payment in 11 instructions under one signature); a route that will not fit one transaction falls back to swap-then-pay. A request can carry an invoice reference, which goes on chain in the memo, so #/jar/<recipient>?ref=<reference> says whether that invoice is paid, part-paid or unpaid from chain data alone and serves as the receipt; a link opened twice says it has already been paid before the button is offered. Requests are priced in a token or in US dollars, converted at the Cookiescan price when the payer opens the link; a tip jar leaves the amount open. The payer can add 1% for the Cookie Jar, Cookie Chain's community treasury, as a second transfer in the same transaction, and the treasury's own jar page lists the gift. An agent on cookie-mcp can pay the same link with one transfer call, memo included (the memo parameter is cookie-mcp PR #3). There is no backend: the request is base64url-encoded into the URL fragment, which never reaches a server, and every payment is one Cookie Chain transaction (SystemProgram.transfer for native COOK, TransferChecked with an idempotent associated-account create for SPL and Token-2022 tokens) plus an SPL Memo tagged cookiejar:1, so a public jar page rebuilds the recipient's history from getSignaturesForAddress over the wallet and its token accounts and the transactions' own balance deltas. .cook names resolve with a single PDA read against the CookOven registry program, and a name listed for sale on the marketplace is refused rather than paid into escrow. The link, memo and transaction formats are documented in docs/wire-format.md. Cookie Tab holds no keys, takes no fee and deploys no program. 125 unit and render tests run with no network; 25 live checks run against the real chain and ecosystem APIs with no key and no funds.
